title: DiffCrime: A Multimodal Conditional Diffusion Model for Crime Risk Map Inference

problem.claim: Crime risk maps support urban planning and public security management.

gap.claim: Historical crime incidents alone or limited environmental factors are insufficient to accurately model crime occurrences across geographical space.

contributions.claim: DiffCrime is a multimodal conditional diffusion method for inferring crime risk maps from historical crime incidents, satellite imagery, and map imagery.
DiffCrime includes HamNet, a history-gated multimodal denoising network for crime risk map inference.
HamNet uses Gated-based History Fusion to emphasize historical crime data and Time step-Aware Modality Fusion to adaptively control multimodal fusion across diffusion time steps.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate DiffCrime's effectiveness.
DiffCrime is reported to outperform baselines by at least 43% and 31% in RMSE on the two datasets, respectively.

narrative_sequence.summary: Crime risk maps are important for urban planning and public security management.
Existing approaches based on historical incidents or limited environmental factors do not sufficiently model crime occurrences over geographical space.
DiffCrime applies multimodal conditional diffusion to crime risk map inference using historical incidents, satellite imagery, and map imagery.
HamNet combines history-focused fusion with time-step-aware multimodal fusion in the denoising network.
The authors report results from two real-world datasets with RMSE improvements over baselines.

source_observation.claim: The method combines historical crime incidents with satellite and map imagery.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary spatial and historical modalities may address limitations of relying on a single information source.

application.claim: For spatial risk inference, consider integrating temporal event data with multiple environmental or geographic representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which modalities are necessary or whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets.

source_observation.claim: HamNet controls multimodal fusion across diffusion time steps and emphasizes historical crime data.

interpretation.claim: The relative usefulness of conditioning modalities may vary during iterative generation.

application.claim: In iterative multimodal generation, consider scheduling or adapting modality fusion over generation steps.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the fusion schedule, ablations, or conditions under which time-step-aware fusion is beneficial.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, geographic settings, and train-test protocols are not specified.
Baseline identities, exact RMSE values, and statistical uncertainty are not specified.
Implementation details and ablation results are not provided.
